thought.text: Authentication works end-to-end (JWT issued for the superuser). Now let me test QGIS WMS GetCapabilities **with** the auth token (proving the forward_auth → QGIS → PostgreSQL read path):

reasoning_content:
Authentication is working end-to-end: JWT login returns HTTP 200 and a valid access token for the superuser. This proves the following:
- Frontend is being served (via caddy)
- Backend Django API is fully functional (via nginx → caddy)
- Database is migrated, superuser has been created, and fixtures have been loaded
- Authentication (dj-rest-auth) is working

Next, I'll test QGIS WMS GetCapabilities **with** the auth token to prove that the QGIS server + forward_auth + DB read path work.

action.command:
cd /workspace/deployment
TOKEN=$(curl -sk --resolve api.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -X POST https://api.localhost/api/v1/auth/login/ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"username":"admin","password":"Admin!LocalDev123"}' | tr -d '\n' | sed 's/.*"access":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/')
echo "token len: ${#TOKEN}"
echo "=== QGIS WMS GetCapabilities (authenticated) ==="
curl -sk --resolve qgis.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://qgis.localhost/ows/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities" -o /tmp/qgis_caps.xml -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n"
head -c 400 /tmp/qgis_caps.xml; echo
